t: Nothing is left of what you are looking for. The Poets' Fountain stood on a traffic island in Park Lane from 1875 until 1948. It was then removed and is thought to have been destroyed. It was a public fountain with sculptures, and it commemorated Shakespeare, Chaucer and Milton. It was made by members of the Thornycroft family: Hamo, Mary and Thomas. One figure survives, an allegorical figure of Fame, which is displayed in the gardens at Renishaw Hall in Derbyshire.
